paragraphs: Oil smoke behaves unlike any other kind: it is dense enough to be almost opaque, it rolls rather than disperses, and it carries a hard boundary between the black column and clear air. Reproducing that requires a simulation with the right density and dissipation, not a smoke texture on a card.

This set is supplied as cached VDB volumes prepared for Blender, so both the simulation time and the parameter tuning are already done. The fire and the smoke fields come ready to render, retime and light.

At $39 and built to CheckMate specification, it suits film and television visual effects, industrial and disaster documentary content, news and current affairs graphics, motion graphics and games. On sale since 2026.

A pair of water skis is longer, wider and far more curved than snow skis, with deep bindings moulded into the deck and a fin under the tail of each. That fin is the identifying feature and the functional one: without it the ski slides sideways and the whole sport stops working.

The mesh is 37,358 polygons and 38,818 vertices, built entirely from quads with non-overlapping UVs, and ships with 5 texture maps at 2048x2048 carrying the graphics, the rubber bindings and the gloss finish.
At $39 it suits watersports and lakeside visualisation, sporting goods retail renders, summer and holiday advertising, boat and marina scenes, and games. On sale since 2015.

A wide brim straw hat has almost no structure, which is exactly what makes it hard: the brim ripples rather than sitting flat, the crown creases where it is handled, and the ribbon sits in a soft band with the bow falling to one side. A rigid disc on a cylinder reads as a costume prop.

The mesh is minimal at 3,334 polygons and 3,296 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, which suits a subject whose realism comes from the straw texture and the brim curve rather than from density.

At $39 and built to CheckMate specification, it suits fashion and accessory retail renders, resort and travel advertising, summer lifestyle imagery, character set dressing and games. Real-world scale is kept, so it fits a standard head. On sale since 2025.

A conference discussion unit is a wedge on a table with a gooseneck microphone, a touchscreen and voting buttons. The wedge shape angles the screen toward a seated delegate, and the microphone stalk is long enough to reach without leaning - both dictated by hours of sitting rather than by styling.
The mesh is light at 10,880 polygons and 11,346 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, with the screen as a separate surface so an interface can be applied without masking.
At $34 it suits conference and boardroom visualisation, audiovisual equipment marketing, government and institutional interiors, corporate presentation and games. On sale since 2022.

Hawthorn carries three things at once on the same branch: deeply lobed leaves, dense clusters of red berries and long thorns along the wood. It is the thorns that most models omit, and they are the reason the plant has its name and its use as a field boundary for centuries.

The mesh is light at 20,666 polygons and 10,351 vertices in quads and tris. The UVs overlap, which is sensible on a subject built from repeated leaves and berries, and it keeps a branch cheap enough to repeat across a hedge.

A version with fur grooming sits on this page at the same $34. Both suit landscape and garden visualisation, herbal and natural product packaging, botanical illustration, seasonal advertising and games. On sale since 2024.

This generation of phone is remembered for two things: a very large screen at a time when that was still unusual, and a textured plastic back with faux stitching around the edge that imitated a leather notebook. That stitching detail is the identification, and it is entirely a texture problem rather than a geometric one.

The mesh is light at 19,788 polygons and 22,246 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and ships with 25 texture maps at a spread of sizes from 4096x4096 down to 512x512, which is what a set with multiple finishes needs.
At $34 it suits consumer electronics visualisation, technology archive and journalism material, period interior and desk scenes, product renders and games. On sale since 2016.

An airpot dispenser keeps liquid hot without power, using a vacuum flask inside a plastic shell with a pump lid on top. Pressing the lid pushes liquid up a tube and out of the spout, which is why the top is a broad plunger rather than a screw cap, and why these appear at every buffet and office kitchen.
The mesh is light at 8,381 polygons and 4,510 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, with the geometry in the pump lid, the spout and the handle.
At $34 it suits hospitality and catering visualisation, office and break room interiors, buffet and event scenes, kitchenware retail renders and games. On sale since 2023.

A parcel van body is a box with very specific fittings: a roll-up rear shutter, a bulkhead door behind the cab, shelving down both sides and a low step so a driver can get in and out repeatedly all day. This asset is the body alone, which is what a bodybuilder or a fleet specification needs to show.
The mesh is efficient at 60,443 polygons and 60,881 vertices in quads and tris with mixed UV layout, with the geometry in the shutter, the corner posts and the roof ribs.
At $34 and built to StemCell specification, it suits logistics and last mile delivery visualisation, fleet and bodybuilder presentation, courier marketing, urban scenes and games. On sale since 2026.

A shaped case follows the outline of the instrument rather than being an oblong, which saves weight and bulk but means the case itself is instantly recognisable as a violin case even closed. The moulded shell, the carry handle, the latches and the shoulder strap fittings are the visible detail.
The mesh is efficient at 27,792 polygons and 14,215 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, with the geometry in the shell profile, the latches and the strap hardware.

At $34 and built to CheckMate specification, it suits music and instrument retail renders, concert and performance visualisation, education and rehearsal scenes, character set dressing and games. On sale since 2024.

The coin lock is the reason European trolleys end up back in the bay rather than in car parks: a chain from one trolley plugs into the next, and only a returned trolley releases the deposit. That small mechanism on the handle is what distinguishes the type at a glance from an American cart.
The mesh is efficient at 55,966 polygons and 34,445 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, with the geometry in the wire basket, the coin lock housing and the castors.
At $32 it suits supermarket and retail interior visualisation, car park and store exterior scenes, retail marketing, film and television set dressing, and games. On sale since 2023.

This is a desktop scale industrial arm, and the difference from a factory robot is not just size: the joints are exposed, the housings are moulded plastic rather than cast metal, and the whole machine is light enough to be moved by hand. It exists to bring six axis automation to benches rather than to production lines.
The mesh is efficient at 60,904 polygons and 61,803 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, with the density in the joint housings and the cable routing.

At $31 and built to StemCell specification, it suits robotics and automation marketing, laboratory and small manufacturing visualisation, education and maker material, technology presentation and games. On sale since 2025.

Judicial dress is deliberately archaic: a long black robe with wide sleeves, often with bands at the collar, cut in a form that has barely changed in centuries precisely so that the office rather than the person is visible. That anonymity is the design brief, and it is why the garment has almost no shaping.

The mesh is minimal at 3,457 polygons and 3,499 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, which suits a garment that hangs straight and whose interest is in the drape rather than in tailoring.

At $31 and built to StemCell specification, it suits legal and institutional visualisation, courtroom scenes for film and television, education and civics material, editorial illustration and games. On sale since 2025.

A hard cooler is a moulded double wall box with a hinged lid, a drain plug at one end and a swing handle over the top. The proportions are set by what fits inside - bottles standing upright, or ice around them - and the moulded ribs exist to stiffen a large plastic shell that gets sat on constantly.

The mesh runs 27,573 polygons and 27,959 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, and ships with 7 texture maps at a mix of sizes up to 4096x4096 carrying the moulded finish, the branding and the scuffs.
At $29 it suits outdoor and camping visualisation, beach and picnic scenes, beverage and lifestyle advertising, retail renders and games. On sale since 2015.

This bottle is a deliberate reference to an old apothecary flask: a short neck, rounded shoulders, no paper label and text printed directly onto the glass. That absence of a label is the brand's signature and a modelling problem, because everything has to come from the glass surface and the printing rather than from a wrapped decal.

The mesh is minimal at 3,784 polygons and 3,711 vertices in quads and tris with non-overlapping UVs, which is exactly right for glassware where the refractive material and the printing carry all of the realism.
At $29 it suits beverage advertising, bar and restaurant interiors, packaging and label mockups, retail and e-commerce renders, and games. On sale since 2021.
